The House met at eleven of the clock,

REFERENCE BY CHAIR
Re: To Anniversary of Bhopal Gas Tragedy
MR. CHAIRMAN : On the occasion of the anniversary of the Bhopal Gas tragedy,
which took place on the night of 2nd and 3rd December, 1984, on behalf of the House
and on my own behalf, I express my heartfelt sympathies for those who lost their family
members or were rendered disabled.
The tragedy still haunts us in the form of incapacitated people and children born
with deformities. It was indeed a human tragedy of unparalleled magnitude which shocked
the conscience of the world.
The criminal human folly that caused this tragedy has been compounded by
indifferent attitude in subsequent years. It is incumbent on us, morally and legally, to
do our utmost to support the surviving victims in every manner possible.
I am sure the whole House will join me in conveying our heartfelt sympathies to
the people who have suffered due to this man-made tragedy.
I now request Members to rise in their places and observe silence for a minute.
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute.)

OBITUARY REFERENCE
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the passing
away of Shri Inder Kumar Gujral, former Prime Minister of India and a former Member
of this House on the 30th of November, 2012, at the age of 92 years after a prolonged
illness.

[RAJY A SABHA]2 Obituary Reference
Born in December, 1919 at Jhelum, now in Pakistan, Shri Gujral had his education
at Hailey College of Commerce and Forman Christian College, Lahore.
Shri Inder Kumar Gujral, who hailed from a family of freedom fighters, actively
participated in the freedom struggle and underwent imprisonment during the Quit India
Movement.
From his student days, Shri Gujral was active in politics and was President of the
Lahore Students Union. Shri Gujral served as the Vice-President of the New Delhi
Municipal Council for five years, from 1959 to 1964. He was Founder President of
the Delhi Art Theatre. He served as Chancellor of Visva Bharati University, Shanti
Niketan and Maulana Azad National Urdu University, Hyderabad. He was Chairman
of the Indian Council of South Asian Co-operation, President of the Institute of Defence
Studies and Analysis (IDSA), and Chairman of the Government of India Committee
for Promotion of Urdu.
A widely travelled person, Shri Gujral led several Indian Delegations including
Indian Council of South Asian Cooperation in 1961; UNESCO Seminar on ‘Man and
New Communication Systems’, Paris in 1973; UN Session on Environment, Stockholm,
1974; UNESCO Conference on Education and Environment, Tbilisi, 1977; United
Nations General Assembly in 1996 and the UN Special Session of Economic
Development in 1990.
Shri Gujral served as Ambassador of India to erstwhile USSR from 1976 to 1980,
and as Special Envoy to Bulgaria in 1961, and to Gabon, Cameroon, Congo, Chad
and Republic of Central Africa in 1975.
Shri Gujral was a prolific writer and had composed many poetic pieces in Urdu.
Shri Inder Kumar Gujral represented the National Capital Territory of Delhi, and
the States of Punjab and Bihar in this House for three terms, from April, 1964 to April,
1970; from April, 1970 to April, 1976, and again from July, 1992 to March, 1998.
He also served as a Member of the Ninth and Twelfth Lok Sabha.
Shri Gujral served as Union Minister of State in the Ministries of Parliamentary
Affairs, Information and Broadcasting, Communications, Works, Housing and Urban
Development and Planning from 1967 to 1976. He served as Minister of External Affairs
from 1989 to 1990 and again from 1996 to 1997 and as the Minister for Water Resources
in 1996.
Shri Inder Kumar Gujral served as the Leader of the House in the Rajya Sabha
from June, 1996 to November, 1996 and again from April, 1997 to March, 1998. He

also served as Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee
on Commerce from 1993 to 1996.
Shri Gujral occupied the Office of the Prime Minister of India from April, 1997
to March, 1998.
In the passing away of Shri Inder Kumar Gujral, the country has lost a veteran
freedom fighter, a great statesman, an able administrator, an erudite scholar and a
distinguished parliamentarian.
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of respect
to the memory of the departed.
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute)
MR. CHAIRMAN: Secretary-General will convey to the members of the bereaved
family our sense of profound sorrow and deep sympathy.
As a mark of respect to the memory of Shri Inder Kumar Gujral, former Prime
Minister, the House stands adjourned till 11.00 a.m. on Tuesday, the 4th of December,
2012.
The House then adjourned at nine minutes past eleven of the clock till eleven of
